newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian bull market in stocks; index sets record.
newsitem.headline: Russian bull market in stocks; index sets record.

text.p: A scramble by tense investors to buy Russian stocks is sending the market charging again, even though it has already jumped 50 percent so far this year, and traders say they cannot predict when it will pause for breath.

An outburst of activity, which began Monday after a two-week pause propelled the Russian Trading System index to a record 312.60 points on Tuesday from 304.90 on Monday. At the end of 1996, the stock index stood at less than 200 points.
"This is it," said Peter Kizenko, head of equities trading at ING Barings in Moscow, adding that investor funds were chasing a limited number of shares. "Stock appears -- stock gets taken."
Second-tier utilities and telecommumication companies led the field.
"The orders are not as price-sensitive these days," Kizenko said. "That shows a different kind of money."

Trading volumes, which were $50 million Tuesday, have not jumped significantly. But traders said the market had been frenzied as investors who had hoped for better buying opportunities in a correction began actively acquiring shares.
Domestic investors were bidding up stocks, including commercial banks moving from the Treasury bill market where many yields, unadjusted for inflation, have fallen since last year.

The International Monetary Fund's decision to release $650 million in delayed funds to Russia on Friday and Russia's recent inclusion on the International Finance Corporation index had also helped, traders said.
Worries about President Boris Yeltsin's health have receded.

"It is going to take a significant political event to take down this market," said James Fenkner, head of research at CentreInvest Securities. "There is just too much momentum and sourcing of shares is difficult."
Technical analysis which had predicted the timing of the new rally also predicted it would last one to two weeks and would hit resistance when the stock index neared 330, he said.
Other traders said the rally could last longer and did not expect a significant downturn, given limited liquidity and demand for shares in a seller's market.
